findings.claim: The bot-only test changes the meaning of `publish --pr` for anyone whose GH_TOKEN is not a bot's, and the plan does not say so. The subcommand's help (action/agent.py:1340-1350) says that with --pr it posts one comment "and replace[s] it on the next run", and asks only for "gh and GH_TOKEN". Run by a person, or with a machine user's personal access token, its own comment has `user.type == "User"`. Under O1 it never matches that comment, so every run posts another one: the one-comment promise breaks without a word. The action itself is fine, since action.yml:272 always passes `github.token` (github-actions[bot], type Bot), and a GitHub App token also posts as type Bot. But the plan's claim that the test covers "a GitHub App token alike" leaves out the PAT case. Pick one: state in the plan that replacement needs a bot token and add the help text (action/agent.py, already in touches) to O1, or pick a test that also finds a person-token's own comment. Matching the token's own login does not work, because `gh api user` returns 403 for GITHUB_TOKEN.
